data.name: Nevrosa: Escape
data.detailed_description:
Primal Ritual Steam Page Launched


Acerca do jogo

Nevrosa é um jogo do gênero "escape da sala" (Escape Room) , misturando em si as enigmas fascinantes, as cenas de batalhas quentes e os elementos de horror. O objetivo é sair do laboratório, cheio de máquinas misteriosas e criaturas sinistros. Vários finais dependendo da sua escolha.


  • Imersão Total — Uma tecnologia de movimento de jogador única permite que você se mova livremente dentro de sua área de jogo, ajustando a cena para se adequar a você.
  • A jogabilidade única é uma combinação de quebra-cabeças, tiroteios, monstros horríveis e jornadas místicas para outros mundos.
  • Estilística Art Deco, repleta de dezenas de detalhes no interior e nos móveis, uma incrível atmosfera de sigilosidade e mistério no mais alto nível de gráfica.
  • Artefato sinistro: por que ele está te seguindo? Ele sussurra algo ou isso simplesmente parece?
  • Trilha sonora sinfônica com tecnologia de som 360 e o som cuidadosamente selecionado.
  • Finais diferentes: Você decide como acabar com esse pesadelo.

The Demo will be made ASAP and there is always FREE Nevrosa: Prelude for you:



O jovem Sr. Conway herda uma propriedade da família em algum lugar no norte da Europa. Seu avô, William Conway, desapareceu há alguns anos e era conhecido como um talentoso inventor e apaixonado por objetos de arte de Art Deco.

Infelizmente, a doença psiquiátrica familiar de Conway atingio o idoso e tem sido particularmente progressiva nos últimos anos, então não há absolutamente nenhuma informação sobre eles.
Explorando uma antiga mansão, você se depara com o laboratório do avô, onde sua curiosidade leva a conseqüências completamente inesperadas ...
Agora você precisa encontrar um caminho para sair da armadilha, desvendar o mistério do desaparecimento do avô e não enlouquecer por causa do que vai começar a acontecer ao seu redor e derrotar a doença.

Você permanecerá o ser humano até o fim?

Nós preparamos algo incomum para todos os possuidores de capacetes de Realidade Virtual:
  • Movendo a pé! sem teleportes, touchpad-deslocamentos ou outras tentativas de enganar a consciência - vá naturalmente, como na vida real, e o jogo em si irá moldar a cena para você. É necessário um mínimo de 1,5 x 2 metros.
  • O corpo e as mãos do jogador! Nós não escondemos seus membros de você. Todos os itens podem ser pegas no mão da maneira mais simples possível e os dedos os cobrem naturalmente e como na vida real. Então, mantenha-os longe de objetos pontiagudos!
  • Trilha Sonora Sinfônica Impressionante

reviews.review:
Nevrosa: Escape is a virtual reality horror adventure built around escape-room puzzles, physical interaction, psychological tension, and supernatural mystery. Developed and published by GexagonVR, it places players inside the unsettling laboratory of William Conway, an eccentric scientist whose disappearance is tied to disturbing experiments and a troubled family history. Instead of relying entirely on conventional jump scares, the game creates unease through environmental details, strange machinery, unexplained events, and the growing suspicion that something is seriously wrong with both the laboratory and the protagonist.

The laboratory is one of the strongest parts of the experience. Its art deco-inspired design gives the environment considerably more character than a generic abandoned facility, and practically every corner encourages investigation. Mechanical devices, mysterious artifacts, scientific equipment, mirrors, and other interactive objects contribute to the feeling that the room itself is an elaborate puzzle. The player must observe the surroundings carefully, manipulate objects, understand mechanisms, and determine how apparently unrelated clues fit together. Because everything is experienced through VR, simple activities such as reaching for an object or examining a strange device become more immersive than they would through traditional mouse and keyboard controls.

The puzzle design is accompanied by a darker supernatural element. Mirrors connect the laboratory to the mysterious Mist world, while strange creatures and unexplained phenomena gradually turn what begins as an escape attempt into something more disturbing. The game frequently creates uncertainty about what is real, what might be supernatural, and what could be connected to the Conway family's mental condition. This ambiguity gives the story an interesting psychological dimension without requiring lengthy exposition. Environmental clues and discoveries gradually reveal information about William Conway, his experiments, and the events that transformed his laboratory into such a dangerous place.

Horror is integrated directly into exploration rather than existing only through scripted scares. Players may encounter threatening situations while investigating the environment, and the possibility of danger makes concentrating on puzzles considerably more stressful. There are also darker themes involving rituals, blood, dangerous objects, and hostile creatures. These elements give Nevrosa: Escape more variety than a straightforward virtual escape room, although players primarily interested in relaxed puzzle solving may find the horror interruptions somewhat distracting. Conversely, those expecting a constant action-oriented horror game should understand that careful observation and puzzle solving remain central to the experience.

Physical interaction is particularly important because the game was designed specifically for room-scale VR. Rather than treating virtual reality as an optional display mode, Nevrosa: Escape incorporates movement and hand interaction directly into its design. Players physically move around the available area, manipulate objects, operate mechanisms, and interact with the environment using tracked controllers. Having visible virtual hands and a body also strengthens the sense of presence. This approach can make the laboratory feel remarkably tangible, but it comes with practical limitations. Adequate room space and compatible PC VR equipment are essential, making the game much less accessible than a conventional desktop horror title.

The audio presentation also deserves recognition. Positional sound is especially effective in virtual reality because noises coming from outside the player's field of vision can immediately create anxiety. Combined with the game's music and mechanical environmental sounds, this allows quieter moments to remain tense even when nothing is directly attacking the player. The visual presentation similarly benefits from its unusual combination of vintage scientific equipment, art deco styling, supernatural imagery, and gloomy lighting. It may not compete technically with modern high-budget VR productions, but its coherent artistic direction gives it a memorable personality.

Replayability is strengthened by multiple endings that can change depending on decisions and actions made during the adventure. Escape-room games often struggle with replay value because knowing the puzzle solutions dramatically reduces the challenge of a second playthrough. Alternative outcomes provide an additional incentive to return, experiment with different choices, and pay closer attention to details that may have seemed insignificant the first time. The underlying mystery also benefits from replaying because previously confusing environmental clues can make more sense once the broader story is understood.

Nevrosa: Escape is not without limitations. Puzzle progression can occasionally slow the horror pacing when a solution is difficult to recognize, while its specialized room-scale design restricts who can comfortably play it. Its relatively focused scope also means players expecting a lengthy campaign may find the experience smaller than a traditional horror adventure. Still, these limitations are balanced by a clear understanding of what makes VR effective: physical presence, environmental interaction, spatial sound, and the discomfort of having threatening events seemingly occur within the player's own surroundings.

Steam Deck compatibility is effectively unsupported for normal play. Nevrosa: Escape is a VR-only experience requiring SteamVR-compatible virtual reality hardware and tracked controllers, while the Steam Deck does not natively provide the required VR setup. It should therefore not be purchased with the expectation of playing directly on the Deck's built-in screen and controls.

Overall, Nevrosa: Escape is a distinctive combination of escape-room problem solving and supernatural VR horror. Its atmospheric laboratory, tactile interactions, unsettling Conway family mystery, multiple endings, and effective use of positional audio demonstrate a game designed around virtual reality rather than merely adapted to it. Its mandatory VR hardware and room-scale requirements significantly narrow its audience, but players with the appropriate setup who enjoy puzzles mixed with psychological horror can find a compact, immersive, and appropriately unnerving adventure.

Rating: 7/10
